content:
samir: Quick RFC follow-up — I'm rethinking the demotion/evict path to avoid global leases. idea: per-prefix causal id (cid) + epoch baked into the handoff so we can deterministically reject concurrent demotes without extra quorum RPCs. lightweight, <1 RTT in happy path.

liz: can you sketch the failure sequence you want to avoid?

samir: sure. imagine two nodes A/B both think they can demote same prefix at epoch=5. if they race we can get double-demote or a brief window where neither has ownership. sketch: 
```
A: demote(pfx, epoch=5, cid=42)
B: demote(pfx, epoch=5, cid=43)
A -> B: demote-prepare{epoch:5,cid:42}
B sees local cid=43 (higher) -> rejects A -> both spin/retry -> chaos
```
The cid is monotonic per-node, we compare (epoch,cid,node-id) lexicographically. No extra leader/quorum.

ton: Why not deterministic tie-breaker by node-id only? We already have node-id ordering.

samir: node-id tie-breaker works for simultaneous single-shot demotes but doesn't capture happened-before (retries). cid gives us causal progress so retries don't falsely win. Also helps in telemetry: we can see how often higher-cid wins.

maria: My worry: we're adding metadata to the hot path (8-16 bytes). is that acceptable? also GC of cid map after epoch rollover?

samir: cost is a few bytes per handoff header; we already do epoch + token. I think it's negligible compared to payload. for GC: when epoch increments we drop old entries; add small TTL.

jen: operationally, how do we surface anomalies? we should emit a demote_conflict counter + last_conflict_sample with prefix id so SRE can triage.

samir: yep plan: metric demote_conflicts{prefix,loser_node,winner_node,epoch} and a trace span that includes cid values.

liz: can we avoid races entirely with deterministic backoff windows (node-id * base_delay) so only one actively retries immediately?

ton: that's clever but brittle: scheduling jitter on overloaded nodes could still cause overlap. prefer a correctness-first tie-breaker + optional backoff.

ops-bot: deploy-note: prefetch-demote-prototype rolled to canary (region-us-east) at 2026-02-12T12:03Z.

samir: proposed next steps: 1) small prototype in runtime that adds (epoch,cid,node-id) comparisons in demote/handback path; 2) unit test that flaps 1000 concurrent demotes and asserts single demote outcome; 3) telemetry + simple alert when conflicts > 0.1% of demotes.

maria: add a CI-only stress test too (separate job). if it looks stable we can add to RFC follow-up and mark low-risk.

liz: I'm OK with this approach. can you also add a note about recovery after network partition (how we catch up missing cids)?

samir: yes — recovery: when a node rejoins, it accepts the highest epoch seen and ratchets its cid to max(local_cid, observed_cid)+1. will document.

tony: ack.

liz: ack.

samir: I'll push a short PR and append this to the RFC as "cid-based demote tie-breaking". thanks all :thumbsup:
